data.title: The Art of Assembly Language (2010)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 《The Art of Assembly Language》是一本关于汇编语言编程的指南，现已由No Starch Press出版。本书适用于希望深入学习汇编语言编程的读者，并通过HLA（High-Level Assembly）语言进行教学。书中详细介绍了HLA程序的基本结构、数据声明、控制结构以及标准库的使用，并提供了多个示例程序。此外，本书还涵盖了数制系统、数据组织、逻辑运算、位操作以及浮点数和字符的表示方法。对于80x86处理器的寻址模式、内存组织、堆栈段和动态内存分配等内容，书中也进行了深入讲解。通过结合理论与实践，帮助读者全面掌握汇编语言编程技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用HLA（High-Level Assembly）的书籍及其在学习和实际应用中的价值

不同观点：
• [pan69] 认为书的内容写得很好，但使用HLA是一个让人反感的点，他更希望书籍专注于标准的厂商编译器，而不是HLA。
• [gtirloni] 表示对新版书籍的期待因为HLA而被打破，学习HLA感觉像是在学习一个更差的C语言，无法提升对汇编本身的理解。
• [anta40] 认为HLA基本上已经被抛弃，适合编译器开发者，但不适合学习汇编编程基础的人，因为HLA编译器仍需要依赖MASM、FASM等汇编器来构建可执行文件。
• [singularity2001] 提到自己喜欢用汇编做小补丁来修改程序，但随着代码签名的普及，这种乐趣已经消失。他不追求极致优化，因此汇编在常规开发中的相关性为零。
• [discardable_dan] 建议将汇编学习游戏化，比如通过Zachtronics的游戏来学习，认为这种体验更好，尤其在书籍内容不够吸引人的情况下。
• [0xSKOOMA] 推荐阅读《Learn to Program with Assembly: Foundational Learning for New Programmers》，认为这本书更现代化，对初学者友好。
• [billmcneale] 认为推荐的书籍内容更像是一个功能较弱的C语言版本，如果要走这条路，还不如学习LLVM。
• [revskill] 关心是否有一个Docker环境可以运行书中的汇编代码。

补充讨论：
• HLA的实用性和学习价值存在争议，部分人认为它不适合初学者或实际应用。
• 有人对现代化的汇编学习资源有需求，并提出了替代方案和学习路径。
• 对于汇编在现代开发中的应用场景和相关性，存在不同看法，特别是在代码签名和优化方面的影响。
• 有人提议通过游戏化方式提高学习汇编的兴趣和体验。

data.title: Raspberry Pi Lidar Scanner
data.author: Venn1
data.article_summary: PiLiDAR是一个DIY的360° 3D全景扫描仪项目，基于Raspberry Pi和LDRobot的LiDAR传感器（如LD06、LD19、STL27L）。其核心功能包括自定义串行驱动、CRC数据完整性检查、硬件PWM校准、2D实时可视化和导出（numpy或CSV格式）。全景功能通过Hugin软件将鱼眼照片拼接成6K的360°全景图，而3D场景功能则通过角度和偏移从2D平面构建3D场景，支持Open3D可视化和多种格式导出。项目还涉及NEMA17步进电机、A4988驱动器和3D打印部件等硬件配置，以及GPIO中断、电源管理和I2C配置等设置步骤。目前项目仍在开发中，初步结果包括单次扫描和基础点云处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个硬件产品的 bill of materials（材料清单）、成本估算、技术细节和应用场景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **godelski**：建议在材料清单中提供链接和估算成本，即使是粗略的数字，也能帮助人们决定是否自行尝试。他还强调文档记录的重要性，以减少日后麻烦，尤其是在工程项目中。他还提供了一些具体部件的示例价格。
• **Animats**：指出该扫描仪的最大范围为12米，超过这个距离成本会显著上升。认为该设备适用于小型机器人和辅助传感器，但长距离LIDAR仍很难实现。
• **joeevans1000**：对项目的精确度数据感兴趣，特别是超过10米的精确度，并提到FARO扫描仪的精度。他还询问了商业使用的贡献要求。
• **amelius**：寻求一种便宜的方法来测量约300mm距离上10微米的精度，询问是否有相关方案。
• **politelemon**：对项目的3D展示效果表示赞赏，但指出鼠标控制的困惑，感觉不自然。
• **mannyv**：建议可以从eBay或Goodwill上的机器人吸尘器中获取相关部件。
• **abraae**：感慨现代技术的发展，使得个人能够创造出如此先进的技术。
• **heljara**：讨论了LIDAR在室内扫描和建模中的应用，关注点包括软件后处理、点云合并、遮挡问题、以及与 photogrammetry 的比较。
• **itissid**：认为该技术对家庭装修项目有帮助，特别是生成难以到达的地方的点云地图。
• **badmonster**：关注PiLiDAR在大型户外数据集上的可扩展性和性能，询问是否在SemanticKITTI或nuScenes等数据集上进行了基准测试。
• **donatj**：表示该项目正是他几周前寻找的，但仍在犹豫选择哪种LIDAR扫描仪。
• **Aspos**：质疑使用GY-521和MPU6050 IMU的原因，认为它们在精度和性能上不够理想。
• **Havoc**：关心这些传感器的安全性，特别是对眼睛的影响。
• **mannyv**：提出如何避免自己的LIDAR干扰他人的LIDAR的问题。

补充讨论：
• 项目的成本和精确度是讨论的重点，许多人对实际应用中的性能和商业使用条件感兴趣。
• 有人关注技术细节，如IMU的选择和LIDAR的干扰问题，显示出对硬件实现的深入兴趣。
• 有人提出控制和操作的用户体验问题，如鼠标控制的自然性。
• 讨论还涉及到不同应用场景，如家庭装修、室内建模和大型户外数据集的处理。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在LIDAR的精确度和成本之间的平衡，以及硬件选择的合理性（如IMU的选择）。
• 另外，如何避免LIDAR之间的干扰也是一个技术上的争议点。

Setup
Power Button (Wakeup & Shutdown)
Wakeup is hardwired to Pin 3
enable gpio-shutdown
echo "dtoverlay=gpio-shutdown" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
if necesessary:
sudo nano /etc/systemd/logind.conf
HandlePowerKey=poweroff
enable i2c-GPIO for GY-521 Accelerometer
GY-521 (MPU 6060): Accelerometer, Gyroscope and thermometer
i2c adress: 0x68
Since GPIO3 is hardwired to the Power Button, we need to use i2c-GPIO to map custom i2c pins (
tutorial
). Unlike serial is not getting crossed, so we connect SDA-SDA and SCL-SCL.
SDA: GPIO22
SCL: GPIO27
disable ic2_arm and enable i2c-gpio in /boot/firmware/config.txt
dtparam=i2c_arm=off
dtoverlay=i2c-gpio,bus=3,i2c_gpio_delay_us=1,i2c_gpio_sda=22,i2c_gpio_scl=27
search for devices on i2c bus 3:
sudo i2cdetect -y 3
Power LED and CPU fan
# CPU fan at lower temp
echo "dtoverlay=gpio-fan,gpiopin=4,temp=45000" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
# Power LED Heartbeat:
echo "dtparam=pwr_led_trigger=timer" >> /boot/firmware/config.txt
Scan Button: register GPIO interrupt
make script executable:
chmod +x gpio_interrupt.py
create new service for autostart
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/pilidar.service
content:
[Unit]
Description=PiLiDAR-Button
After=network.target
[Service]
Type=simple
User=pi
Environment=LG_WD=/tmp
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /home/pi/PiLiDAR/gpio_interrupt.py
Restart=no
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
reload daemon, enable and start service:
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable pilidar.service
sudo systemctl start pilidar.service
check service if necessary:
sudo systemctl status pilidar.service
set Permission for UART on Raspberry Pi
temporary solution:
sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
old solution: make it permanent by disabling password for chmod:
sudo visudo
pi ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0
then execute the
temporary
solution from python:
import subprocess
command = "sudo chmod a+rw /dev/ttyS0"
process = subprocess.Pop

• **Animats**：指出该扫描仪的最大范围为12米，超过这个距离成本会显著上升。认为该设备适用于小型机器人和辅助传感器，但长距离LIDAR仍很难实现。
• **joeevans1000**：对项目的精确度数据感兴趣，特别是超过10米的精确度，并提到FARO扫描仪的精度。他还询问了商业使用的贡献要求。
• **amelius**：寻求一种便宜的方法来测量约300mm距离上10微米的精度，询问是否有相关方案。
• **politelemon**：对项目的3D展示效果表示赞赏，但指出鼠标控制的困惑，感觉不自然。
• **mannyv**：建议可以从eBay或Goodwill上的机器人吸尘器中获取相关部件。
• **abraae**：感慨现代技术的发展，使得个人能够创造出如此先进的技术。
• **heljara**：讨论了LIDAR在室内扫描和建模中的应用，关注点包括软件后处理、点云合并、遮挡问题、以及与 photogrammetry 的比较。
• **itissid**：认为该技术对家庭装修项目有帮助，特别是生成难以到达的地方的点云地图。
• **badmonster**：关注PiLiDAR在大型户外数据集上的可扩展性和性能，询问是否在SemanticKITTI或nuScenes等数据集上进行了基准测试。
• **donatj**：表示该项目正是他几周前寻找的，但仍在犹豫选择哪种LIDAR扫描仪。
• **Aspos**：质疑使用GY-521和MPU6050 IMU的原因，认为它们在精度和性能上不够理想。
• **Havoc**：关心这些传感器的安全性，特别是对眼睛的影响。
• **mannyv**：提出如何避免自己的LIDAR干扰他人的LIDAR的问题。

补充讨论：
• 项目的成本和精确度是讨论的重点，许多人对实际应用中的性能和商业使用条件感兴趣。
• 有人关注技术细节，如IMU的选择和LIDAR的干扰问题，显示出对硬件实现的深入兴趣。
• 有人提出控制和操作的用户体验问题，如鼠标控制的自然性。
• 讨论还涉及到不同应用场景，如家庭装修、室内建模和大型户外数据集的处理。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在LIDAR的精确度和成本之间的平衡，以及硬件选择的合理性（如IMU的选择）。
• 另外，如何避免LIDAR之间的干扰也是一个技术上的争议点。

data.title: Unpowered SSD endurance investigation finds data loss and performance issues
data.author: progval
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了SSD在断电情况下长时间存放数据时可能出现的数据丢失问题，尤其是用于备份或存储重要文件时。TechTuber HTWingNut进行了一项实验，测试了四块SATA SSD在断电两年后的数据完整性。实验包括两块“全新”和两块“磨损”的SSD，其中磨损的驱动器写入数据量远超其耐久度额定值。第一年的测试没有发现问题，但第二年测试显示“磨损”的SSD出现了文件损坏和性能下降，而“全新”的SSD尽管数据完整，但错误校正值较高，暗示潜在问题。文章提醒用户定期刷新备份以防数据丢失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SSD的耐用性及其作为长期存储介质的适用性

不同观点：
• jauntywundrkind：提到即使是廉价SSD，其实际耐用性也可能高于其标定值，但温度敏感性仍然是一个需要考虑的因素。计划将系统放在炎热的阁楼中，考虑进行年度数据刷新以确保数据完整性。
• gnabgib：引用了其他讨论，提供更多关于SSD耐用性的背景信息和相关讨论。
• ksec：指出USB闪存存在数据位翻转和损坏问题，并询问是否有解决方案。
• rkagerer：表示不会购买无品牌SSD，基于过去的经验发现这些SSD存在数据损坏问题，并开发了验证工具。
• bityard：认为SSD不适合长期存储是显而易见的观点。
• stego-tech：认为SSD作为冷存储风险较大，驱动器使用寿命和未通电时间影响其可靠性，并呼吁推出面向消费者的经济型LTO驱动器。
• ein0p：认同SSD不适合长期冷存储，并指出需要定期通电以保持数据完整性，同时提醒加密硬件的闪存也有类似问题。
• csdvrx：建议使用传统硬盘进行长期存储，并提供特定需求下选择SLC驱动器或修改固件的建议，提醒注意新技术的测试不足问题。
• jeffbee：指出编程温度对SSD耐用性的影响，认为温度变化会影响实验结果。
• 0manrho：认为使用廉价、高度磨损的SSD得出的结论不具代表性，强调需要通过规模化使用和理解存储阵列概念来提高可靠性，同时区分不同类型和品质的闪存驱动器。

补充讨论：
• SSD的温度敏感性和定期通电对数据保持的影响被多次提到，是讨论中的一个关键点。
• 不同类型的闪存（如MLC/TLC/QLC）和品牌差异（无品牌、白牌、企业级SSD）在讨论中被强调，影响SSD性能和可靠性的评估。
• 提出了对经济型LTO驱动器的需求，反映出消费者和爱好者对稳定备份解决方案的渴望。
• 对廉价SSD的讨论中，强调了需要通过规模化使用和系统设计来提升其可靠性和性能。

43739028.article_content:
(Image credit: HTWingNut)
You may not know it, but SSDs will lose data after a period of time if they are simply left unplugged, which can be a serious threat to your data if you store backups or precious files on unplugged SSDs. A year-two update on the
how long can SSDs store data unpowered
video series is another reminder about the importance of regularly refreshing your backups with a bit of juice. The tests consist of storing data on an SSD and then leaving it unplugged for years to see the impact on the stored data.
As a reminder, an SSD's endurance rating is calculated based on how long it can store data if left unplugged after a certain amount of data has been written, hence the importance of this testing.
TechTuber HTWingNut is back with a report on his modest experiment involving a quartet of SATA SSDs. The key finding was that the two-year-old, well-worn drive exhibited noticeable performance degradation and was affected by a handful of corrupt files. These are signs that this particular SSD was on its way to silicon heaven. HTWingNut's video is an update on an episode from a year earlier, and further updates are promised.
You may like
World Backup Day: A reminder to protect against data loss
Seagate hard drive controversy persists as scammers discover methods to alter reliability metrics
How Long Can SSD Store Data Unpowered? Year 2 Update - YouTube
Watch On
The four tested 'Leven JS-600' branded SSDs are basically bog-standard no-name units. HTWingNut says they are all TLC SSDs of 128GB capacity and rated to withstand 60 TB of written data. Every drive has 100GB of files containing random data, with hash values for all the content provided for later verification.
The two 'Fresh' samples have barely been used; perhaps only the 100GB data set was put on there and verified, and that's it. Meanwhile, the 'Worn' drives have been subjected to 280 terabytes of written data churn, much more than their rated 60 Terabytes Written (TBW) endurance rating..
If you watch the previous
year-one video
, you will have seen there were no issues with either 'Worn' or 'Fresh' drives. However, time has now taken its toll. Let's take a look at the year-two samples in turn.
'Fresh' SSD tests
The data on this SSD, which hadn't been used or powered up for two years, was 100% good on initial inspection. All the data hashes verified, but it was noted that the verification time took a smidgen longer than two years previously. HD Sentinel tests also showed good, consistent performance for a SATA SSD.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
Digging deeper, all isn't well, though. Firing up Crystal Disk Info, HTWingNut noted that this SSD had a Hardware ECC Recovered value of over 400. In other words, the disk's error correction had to step in to fix hundreds of data-based parity bits.
Seeing these errors means "the SSD is on its way out," according to HTWingNut. Indeed, if there is anything iffy about your data storage integrity, it is at least a warning. However, the errors could also have something to do with the drive being left unpowered for two years.
(Image credit: HTWingNut)
'Worn' SSD tests
As the worn SSD's data was being verified, there were already signs of performance degradation. The hashing audit eventually revealed that four files were corrupt (hash not matching). Looking at the elapsed time, it was observed that this operation astonishingly took over 4x longer, up from 10 minutes and 3 seconds to 42 minutes and 43 seconds.
Further investigations in HD Sentinel showed that three out of 10,000 sectors were bad and performance was 'spiky.' Returning to Crystal Disk Info, things look even worse. HTWingNut notes that the uncorrectable sectors count went from 0 to 12 on this drive, and the hardware ECC recovered value went from 11,745 before to 201,273 after tests on the day.
Some takeaways
In summary, the year-one fresh and well-worn drives had no issues. However, the year-two heavily worn SSD had file corruption and performance was poor. The so-called fresh drive was still good, but ECC figures still raised concern. Come back in late 2025 for the next update from HTWingNut.
We also want to say this is a very small test sample, highlighted out of our interest in the topic rather than for its hard empirical data. I have also experienced SSD data loss after leaving a Mini PC unpowered for just six months or so at my pied-à-terre in Taiwan. On return, Windows refused to boot or be repaired, but a reformat and reinstall seemed to return everything to normal.

data.title: An image of the Australian desert illuminates satellite pollution
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 摄影师Joshua Rozells在澳大利亚Pinnacles Desert拍摄星空时，意外发现大量卫星轨迹污染了照片。他将343张照片合成一张图片，展示了日益严重的卫星污染问题。自2019年SpaceX启动Starlink项目以来，已有超过10,000颗卫星升空，且计划发射更多。天文学家警告，卫星数量激增加剧光污染，影响天文研究。尽管这些卫星提供重要数据，但缺乏监管可能导致问题恶化。一些组织，如国际天文学联合会的保护暗静天空中心，正呼吁规范和保护夜空。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：卫星对天文观测和摄影的影响，以及是否应该对卫星数量和光污染进行监管

不同观点：
• yellowapple认为，尽管卫星提供了重要数据，但过多的卫星会加剧光污染并影响天文研究。他建议将天文台放置在轨道上，以减少这些问题，而不是一味指责卫星。
• pixelesque以自身经验说明，在Starlink发射之前，拍摄天文照片更容易，而现在需要通过复杂的多次曝光和后期处理来去除卫星轨迹，尽管这种方法可能有助于提高照片质量，但也增加了工作量。
• ag56质疑所谓的“问题”到底是什么，认为能够拍摄到这样的照片表明了技术的进步，并对反对卫星的观点持怀疑态度。
• trebligdivad虽然承认卫星网格对天文观测有负面影响，但仍对其视觉效果表示赞赏。
• perilunar认为城市的光污染比卫星的影响更大，应更关注城市光污染问题。
• jfengel承认这个问题对天文和摄影有影响，但觉得通过大量照片拼接来解决问题的工作量过大，削弱了其说服力。
• madmask好奇未接触部落对Starlink的看法，暗示卫星对不同文化群体的潜在影响。
• nntwozz幽默地提到可能出现太空广告，指出除非有监管，否则这种现象可能出现。
• WalterBright提出简单地将卫星涂成黑色以减少其可见性的方案。
• macinjosh认为为偏远地区提供互联网比方便天文摄影更重要，强调了卫星的实际社会效益。
• sandspar支持卫星带来的好处，认为在可预见的未来，这些好处值得付出一些代价。
• kofianon则提出一个创业想法，即发射专门拍摄清洁夜空照片的卫星，以订阅模式盈利。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于卫星对天文观测和摄影的影响程度，以及是否应优先考虑这些影响与卫星带来的社会经济效益之间的平衡。
• 讨论中还涉及是否需要更多的法规来限制卫星数量和光污染，以及技术解决方案（如将卫星涂成黑色或通过后期处理去除卫星轨迹）的可行性。
• 不同参与者对美学价值、技术进步和社会效益的优先级存在不同看法。

43737469.article_content:
Photo © Joshua Rozells, shared with permission
A Stunning Image of the Australian Desert Illuminates the Growing Problem of Satellite Pollution
April 18, 2025
Nature
Photography
Grace Ebert
Share
Pin
Email
Bookmark
In January 2021,
Joshua Rozells
ventured out into the Pinnacles Desert in Western Australia, intending to photograph a star trail. But after shooting for more than three hours and reviewing his images, he realized that the light patterns he captured weren’t what he had hoped for.
“There were satellite trails visible in almost every single photo,” he wrote on
Instagram
. “Instead of trying to get rid of them for a star trail, I decided to put the satellite trails together into a single image to show how polluted the night sky is becoming.”
Stitching together 343 distinct photos, Rozells illuminates a growing problem. When Elon Musk’s SpaceX launched Starlink in 2019, 60 satellites filled the skies, with a race from other companies to follow. That number
has now topped 10,000
, with tens of thousands more in the works. SpaceX alone plans to launch 40,000 more.
Rozells’ composite visually echoes pleas from astronomers, who warn that although satellites collect essential data, the staggering amount filling our skies will only worsen light pollution and our ability to study what lies beyond. Because this industry has little regulation, the problem could go unchecked.
“Thankfully, astronomers across the globe have taken notice of this growing issue and are starting to speak up,” Rozells adds. “Organisations such as the International Astronomical Union’s Center for the Protection of the Dark and Quiet Sky are advocating for the regulation and protection of the night sky.” (via
Kottke
)

• macinjosh认为为偏远地区提供互联网比方便天文摄影更重要，强调了卫星的实际社会效益。
• sandspar支持卫星带来的好处，认为在可预见的未来，这些好处值得付出一些代价。
• kofianon则提出一个创业想法，即发射专门拍摄清洁夜空照片的卫星，以订阅模式盈利。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于卫星对天文观测和摄影的影响程度，以及是否应优先考虑这些影响与卫星带来的社会经济效益之间的平衡。
• 讨论中还涉及是否需要更多的法规来限制卫星数量和光污染，以及技术解决方案（如将卫星涂成黑色或通过后期处理去除卫星轨迹）的可行性。
• 不同参与者对美学价值、技术进步和社会效益的优先级存在不同看法。

43669151.article_content:
Getting your
Trinity Audio
player ready...
A crosswalk button in Redwood City plays a voice professing to be Mark Zuckerberg on April 12. Courtesy Justin Ward.
Crosswalk buttons along the mid-Peninsula were hacked last week so that when pressed, voices professing to be Mark Zuckerberg or Elon Musk began speaking.
Videos taken at locations in Redwood City, Menlo Park and Palo Alto showed various messages that began to play when crosswalk buttons were hit. The voices appeared to imitate how Zuckerberg and Musk sound.
In one video, taken on Saturday morning at the corner of Arguello Street, Broadway and Marshall Street in Redwood City, a voice claiming to be Zuckerberg says that “it’s normal to feel uncomfortable or even violated as we forcefully insert AI into every facet of your conscious experience. And I just want to assure you, you don’t need to worry because there’s absolutely nothing you can do to stop it.”
In another video, taken in downtown Palo Alto early on Saturday morning, a voice claiming to be Musk says that he would “like to personally welcome you to Palo Alto.”
“You know, people keep saying cancer is bad, but have you tried being a cancer? It’s f—— awesome,” the voice goes on to say.
A crosswalk button in Palo Alto plays a voice professing to be Elon Musk on April 12. Courtesy Cynthia Neuwalder.
Another video from downtown Palo Alto shows a voice impersonating Musk saying that he would give the listener a Cybertruck if they became his friend.
A crosswalk button in Menlo Park plays a voice professing to be Mark Zuckerberg on April 12. Courtesy Matthew Schluneker.
“You don’t know the level of depravity I would stoop to just for a crumb of approval,” the voice says. “I mean, let’s be real, it’s not like I had any moral convictions to begin with.”
Over in Menlo Park, a video taken near Meta’s headquarters shows a crosswalk signal with a voice identifying himself as “Zuck” stating how proud he is of “everything we’ve been building together.”
“From undermining democracy, to cooking our grandparents’ brains with AI slop, to making the world less safe for trans people, nobody does it better than us – and I think that’s pretty neat,” the voice says.
Some of the impacted crosswalk buttons in Palo Alto were no longer playing the messages on Saturday morning, one local resident reported.
City of Palo Alto spokesperson Meghan Horrigan-Taylor said on Saturday that city employees determined that 12 downtown intersections were impacted and have disabled the voice announcement feature on the crosswalks until repairs can be made. The tampering may have happened on Friday, Horrigan-Taylor said.
“Other traffic signals in the City were checked and the impact is isolated,” Horrigan-Taylor said. “Signal operations are otherwise unaffected, and motorists are reminded to always exercise caution around pedestrians.”
Redwood City Deputy City Manager Jennifer Yamaguma said on Monday that her city was aware of four locations where crosswalk signals were hacked.
“The unauthorized messages have since been disabled, and staff are evaluating ways to strengthen system protections,” Yamaguma said. “We also want to remind the public that tampering with City infrastructure, including crosswalk signals, is unlawful and poses a safety risk.”
Menlo Park spokesperson Kendra Calvert told this news organization that the affected crosswalks in Menlo Park are operated by the California Department of Transportation and that city-controlled crosswalks were not hacked.
Caltrans spokesperson Jeneane Crawford confirmed that crosswalks operated by the state transportation agency were impacted in Menlo Park and Palo Alto. Caltrans disabled the affected audio on Saturday morning, Crawford said.
“The pedestrian push buttons have been deactivated and crosswalks are currently operating on a timer,” Crawford said on Tuesday. “Caltrans is working with the supplier to determine a course of action so that the crosswalks are fully operational as quickly as possible.”
A Meta spokesperson referred questions to the cities with the impacted crosswalks. Tesla did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

data.title: Electromagnetism as a Purely Geometric Theory
data.author: andyjohnson0
data.article_summary: 本文是一则验证提示，指出为了确保网站安全，用户需要点击下方框以确认自己是人类。若无法完成验证，可点击提供的链接联系支持团队，并附上问题截图。同时给出了联系页面链接和事件ID。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：几何视角下的电磁学和量子现象解释，以及与现有物理理论（如 Higgs 场、规范理论等）的关系。

不同观点：
• **几何解释的有效性**：
  - **mikhailfranco** 引用了 Feynman Checkerboard 和 David Hestenes 的 Zitterbewegung 模型，支持通过几何视角解释电子和光子的行为。
  - **amelius** 认为电磁学可以通过几何框架解释，包括库仑定律和相对论，并提到爱因斯坦已经解决了磁性如何从几何中出现的问题。
  
• **Higgs 场的地位**：
  - **molticrystal** 提到如果 Dirac 方程可以解释为纯几何方程，且无需引入 Higgs 场来解释粒子质量，那么这是否意味着需要重新解释 Higgs 场和 Higgs 玻色子的实验结果。

• **规范理论的关联**：
  - **nimish** 指出 U(1) 规范理论已经通过几何结果解释了电磁学，质疑这是否与讨论的几何解释相符。
  - **Iwan-Zotow** 补充认为讨论中的几何解释涉及非线性电磁学。

• **历史与理论背景**：
  - **nsoonhui** 提到 Kaluza-Klein 理论和爱因斯坦晚年未成功的统一场论尝试，认为这些历史尝试被证明是死胡同，部分原因是当时对强相互作用和弱相互作用不了解。

• **其他物理概念的关联**：
  - **phkahler** 强调洛伦兹力与时空度量结构的直接关系，并指出传统量子力学波函数与电磁波的不同。
  - **ogogmad** 提出几何解释与公理化热力学的潜在联系，两者都涉及微分几何。

• **对几何解释的批评**：
  - **mkoubaa** 将数学物理中的复杂抽象比作某些初级开发者的代码重构，暗示这种几何解释可能过于复杂且难以理解。
  
• **技术性问题与幽默**：
  - **oh_my_goodness** 对 "电荷密度以光速传播" 的说法表示困惑。
  - **rkagerer** 幽默地提到无法越过 "机器人墙"，暗示技术性障碍。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提及电磁学和相对论的关系，尤其是磁场是否可以完全通过电场的相对论效应来描述。
- **hasley** 提问如何学习 Maxwell 方程和电磁场张量，反映了对电磁学几何解释的实际学习需求的关注。

data.title: A unique sound alleviates motion sickness
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: 名古屋大学的研究团队发现了一种独特的声音刺激技术，可以减轻晕动症症状。这种技术使用特定波长的声音（100 Hz的纯音）刺激内耳，只需一分钟的暴露即可有效减少在移动车辆中阅读时产生的眩晕和不适感。研究通过摆动、驾驶模拟器和实际乘车实验验证了效果，结果显示这种声音刺激能够激活交感神经，改善平衡系统功能，缓解恶心和头晕等晕动症症状。该技术的声音强度在日常环境噪音范围内，安全有效，有望应用于航空和航海等多种出行场景。研究发表于《Environmental Health and Preventive Medicine》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：100Hz纯音对运动病的效果及其可行性

不同观点：
• teekert分享了一个个人故事，表明其兄弟因相信抗运动病的设备而产生了效果，暗示了心理作用（安慰剂效应）的可能。
• bhaney对研究持怀疑态度，指出样本量小且未经过盲测，对商标化的尝试感到荒谬，希望看到更严谨的研究。
• jawns关注大学新闻稿中的商业化倾向，质疑其在技术细节披露上的透明度，指出100Hz纯音的商标和潜在的商业利益。
• mcherm认为这个发现非常有前景，但因其简单性和意外性而更加怀疑，强调需要其他研究者的验证。
• Geee指出这并非新概念，之前在VR晕动症和Otolith Labs的研究中已有涉及，并提供了相关链接。
• lambdaone幽默地指出100Hz与50Hz电力系统二次谐波的关系。
• hengheng附和lambdaone，联想到电源哼声的安抚效果。
• 486sx33对发现表示惊叹，并建议开发AirPod应用。
• bombela开玩笑说旧本田思域车震可能是为了缓解运动病。
• jedimastert总结了研究结果，简要说明了100Hz音调的效果。
• modeless提到朋友的严重运动病问题，认为值得尝试这种新方法，并指出运动病问题的普遍性和寻找治愈方法的重要性。
• 8474_s质疑为何必须是100Hz，认为可能是附近频率有最大效果，暗示内耳机制的共振。
• dataviz1000开玩笑说可以在游艇引擎中加入100Hz音以增加卖点。
• hrtk幽默地要求提供播放按钮。
• tempestn分享了个人试验，尽管认为是安慰剂效应，但承认效果，建议在车内阅读时尝试。

补充讨论：
• 研究的可重复性和科学严谨性是争议的焦点，特别是其简单性和意外性增加了怀疑。
• 商业化利益和研究透明度也是讨论的重要方面，特别是商标化和技术细节披露的问题。
• 个人经验和心理作用（安慰剂效应）在讨论中被多次提及，显示了实际应用中的复杂性。

Graduate School of Medicine
Inner ear
Masashi Kato
Nervous system
Neural simulation
Preventive medicine
Takumi Kagawa
A research group led by Takumi Kagawa and Masashi Kato at Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine has discovered that using “a unique sound stimulation technology”—a device that stimulates the inner ear with a specific wavelength of sound—reduces motion sickness. Even a single minute of stimulation reduced the staggering and discomfort felt by people that read in a moving vehicle. The results, published in
Environmental Health and Preventive Medicine
, suggest a simple and effective way to treat this common disorder.
“Our study demonstrated that short-term stimulation using a unique sound called 'sound spice®' alleviates symptoms of motion sickness, such as nausea and dizziness,” Kagawa said. “The effective sound level falls within the range of everyday environmental noise exposure, suggesting that the sound technology is both effective and safe.”
The discovery is an important expansion of recent findings about sound and its effect on the inner ear. Increasing evidence has suggested that stimulating the part of the inner ear associated with balance using a unique sound can potentially improve balance. Using a mouse model and humans, the researchers identified a unique sound at 100 Hz as being the optimal frequency.
“Vibrations at the unique sound stimulate the otolithic organs in the inner ear, which detect linear acceleration and gravity,” Kato explained. “This suggests that a unique sound stimulation can broadly activate the vestibular system, which is responsible for maintaining balance and spatial orientation.”
To test the effectiveness of the devices, they recruited voluntary participants who were exposed to the unique sound. Following the stimulation, motion sickness was induced by a swing, a driving simulator, or riding in a car. The researchers used postural control, ECG readings, and Motion Sickness Assessment Questionnaire results to assess the effectiveness of the stimulation.
Exposure to the unique sound before being exposed to the driving simulator enhanced sympathetic nerve activation. The researchers found symptoms such as “lightheadedness” and “nausea,” which are often seen with motion sickness, were alleviated.
“These results suggest that activation of sympathetic nerves, which are often dysregulated in motion sickness, was objectively improved by the unique sound exposure,” Kato said.
“The health risk of short-term exposure to our unique sound is minimal,” Kagawa said. “Given that the stimulus level is well below workplace noise safety standards, this stimulation is expected to be safe when used properly.”
Their results suggest a safe and effective way to improve motion sickness, potentially offering help to millions of sufferers. The researchers plan to further develop the technology with the aim of practical application for a variety of travel situations including air and sea travel.
The study, “Just 1-min exposure to a pure tone at 100 Hz with daily exposable sound pressure levels may improve motion sickness,” was published in
Environmental Health and Preventive Medicine
on March 25, 2025, at DOI:
10.1265/ehpm.24-00247
.

43740021.article_summary: 名古屋大学的研究团队发现了一种独特的声音刺激技术，可以减轻晕动症症状。这种技术使用特定波长的声音（100 Hz的纯音）刺激内耳，只需一分钟的暴露即可有效减少在移动车辆中阅读时产生的眩晕和不适感。研究通过摆动、驾驶模拟器和实际乘车实验验证了效果，结果显示这种声音刺激能够激活交感神经，改善平衡系统功能，缓解恶心和头晕等晕动症症状。该技术的声音强度在日常环境噪音范围内，安全有效，有望应用于航空和航海等多种出行场景。研究发表于《Environmental Health and Preventive Medicine》期刊。
43740021.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：100Hz纯音对运动病的效果及其可行性

不同观点：
• teekert分享了一个个人故事，表明其兄弟因相信抗运动病的设备而产生了效果，暗示了心理作用（安慰剂效应）的可能。

• jawns关注大学新闻稿中的商业化倾向，质疑其在技术细节披露上的透明度，指出100Hz纯音的商标和潜在的商业利益。
• mcherm认为这个发现非常有前景，但因其简单性和意外性而更加怀疑，强调需要其他研究者的验证。
• Geee指出这并非新概念，之前在VR晕动症和Otolith Labs的研究中已有涉及，并提供了相关链接。
• lambdaone幽默地指出100Hz与50Hz电力系统二次谐波的关系。
• hengheng附和lambdaone，联想到电源哼声的安抚效果。

• modeless提到朋友的严重运动病问题，认为值得尝试这种新方法，并指出运动病问题的普遍性和寻找治愈方法的重要性。
• 8474_s质疑为何必须是100Hz，认为可能是附近频率有最大效果，暗示内耳机制的共振。

data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了关于移动应用位置数据共享的研究，并提供了分析流量的工具和方法。作者最初手动分析了应用的流量，但为了提高效率，开发了一个Python脚本和指南，使分析过程更快、更可扩展。通过该工具，用户可以记录和分析应用流量，发现其中隐藏的信息，特别是与广告技术和位置数据相关的内容。作者还创建了可视化图表，展示广告技术公司域名的分布情况，揭示Unity在移动游戏应用流量中的主导地位。此外，作者提供了一个表单，邀请其他人参与收集和分享应用数据流量的信息，以众包方式扩展研究。整个项目旨在提高人们对应用数据隐私和位置共享问题的认识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过技术手段获取和追踪个人位置信息及隐私数据的现实情况与应对方法

• [3abiton] 回应表示，这类话题时常被讨论，并指出在Android设备上可以使用如XPL-EX或App Manager等工具来阻止此类信息泄露。这表明，虽然隐私泄露问题严重，但仍有技术手段可以进行防护。

• [ddxv] 提供了一个类似的工具（AppGoblin），用于查看移动应用中的追踪器，并提到自己正在开发一个自动化流程来实现类似功能。他提到当前遇到的技术困难，特别是在使用 rooted 模拟器和应用时的问题，并分享了一个GitHub项目链接以寻求建议。

43716704.article_content:
It's been more than 2 months now since my first post on the topic of location data sharing between various 3rd parties came out – in case you haven't seen it, you should definitely start from there:
Everyone knows your location
How I tracked myself down using leaked location data in the in-app ads, and what I found along the way.
tim.sh
tim
Since then I had a chat with a lot of people working in this field – both members of non-profit organisations, fighting for data privacy rights in various countries, and employees of adtech companies, proving my words right or wrong (but mostly right). I was even invited to "
Lock and Code
" podcast to talk about geolocation data and privacy. Ok, enough with the bragging.
I went through the process described in my initial post and decided to make it faster and more scalable: manually going through hundreds of requests in Charles was very cool for research and educational purposes, but it also took me a lot of time to find "interesting" requests coming from a single app.
I've significantly upgraded my approach (though it could definitely be more efficient), and in this post I wanted to share it with you.
TL;DR
I have created a small guide and a Python notebook that allow anyone to record mobile app traffic and find surprising things in it.
Here's
the link to a GitHub repo
with it.
The initial setup takes 10-30 minutes.
Analysis using this algorithm took me about 10 minutes per app - you can definitely dig deeper and get lost for hours if you find something interesting in there..
Follow the
readme
or the guide below if you'd like to try!
I came up with an idea
: it would take me hundreds of hours to go through each app and record the traffic, though I would love to do that – let's not blindly trust some table from the internet, but find out for ourselves.
I copied the Gravy Analytics Google Sheet and created a simple form that you can fill in (no personal info is collected) that writes to that Google Sheet
Link to the table
Look up any app you already have on your phone or just a random one in the table, check if others have commented on it already and record the traffic.
Finally, if you want to help crowdsource the information on the kinds of data the apps from the list collect and share –
fill in the form
:
I found something interesting in the app traffic
Hey! I don’t know how much people will go through with all the instructions and analysis, but since you’re here, you probably already did it and found something. Thanks for being here and doing this. Fill in the form below and your response will be recorded to a shared spreadsheet. PLEASE CHECK ALL OF YOUR INPUTS FOR YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION. This form is set in a way that I collect nothing personal from you (like email or Google account or whatever), but your response will be viewable by virtually anyone - so be aware!
Google Docs
Please edit all the private information in your submission (in case it's there).
Visualising "domain power"
Before jumping into the guide, I wanted to share a few cool-looking visualisations with you.
Long story short: lately I've been obsessed with graph visualisations of things, especially branchy-embedded ones.
While analysing the traffic I found myself curious: how are the adtech companies domains distributed across all of the requests?
So I joined these two together and created a visualisation using
PyVis
that would answer that question:
Here's some context:
Every circle is a domain or a subdomain.
The hierarchy is represented by the inclusion of circles into others.
Example:
o-sdk.ads.unity3d.com
is represented by 3 circles:
o-sdk
inside of
ads
inside of
unity3d
.
Colors represent the app (I analysed 5) that the request corresponds to.
I used low opacities for better visibility, and it turns out that in my mix of colors and their opacities purple is the combination of all of them.
Circle sizes, or masses, represent the frequency: how often did this or that domain appear in the requests data.
See any insights?
Unity
rules the mobile game app traffic scene.
For comparison, the
g / doubleclick
thing is Google Ad Network.
Take a look at it in motion:
I included the code for it –
visualise_domains.ipynb
in the same repo so that you could create the same visualisation out of the data you record.
I also included the
ad_domains.html
file with this sample (mine) graph – simply open it in your browser if you want to play around with it.
I also was curious of the density of the requests – in my last post, I mentioned that hundreds of requests happen in just a few seconds, and now I could finally take a look at them:
Filenames in the legend are flows collected from 5 different games.
I cut it at 60s for better visibility, but obviously there were requests after that as well.
This one is again a different view of the domain power – look at the list on the right.
It should be obvious by now that Unity is the leader in this strange contest – it has the most subdomains called and the most requests mad

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）代理从经验中学习的进展及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [kubb] 对AI代理从经验中学习的技术进步感到兴奋，并设想利用这种技术创建自动化的商业和娱乐工具，例如自动赚钱的SaaS公司和根据个人喜好生成游戏的代理。
• [jgbmlg] 认为在人类智力下降的时代，机器智力的进步具有讽刺意味。
• [0xCE0] 对科学论文缺乏出版日期表示不满，这影响了对论文时效性的判断。
• [artninja1988] 引用了DeepMind的论文，但对“奖励就足够”的假设持怀疑态度，认为固定奖励功能的AI并不等同于通用人工智能（AGI）。
• [quantumHazer] 怀疑此类文章是公关噱头，对文章的实质内容和图表表示不满，并表达了对过度炒作的疲惫感。
• [simianwords] 关注“从经验中学习”是否仍然通过离线的强化学习（RL）实现，而不是自主和持续地学习，并对论文中提到的学习方式产生误解。
• [ChrisArchitect] 引用Richard Sutton的观点，将相关讨论置于更广泛的AI设计框架中。
• [tempodox] 怀疑文章本身是由语言模型（LLM）生成的。
• [numpad0] 认为机器能够实时学习和适应才是AI的真正目标，而不是仅依靠大规模数据集进行训练。
• [kkfx] 认为知识应用的自动化将增加，但知识创造仍需人类参与，并提出谁拥有模型的问题，担心当前由大公司主导的模式可能带来的社会影响。
• [baq] 提醒读者在阅读相关文章或书籍时，应考虑人工智能快速发展的潜在影响，特别是在本世纪20年代末可能发生的技术突破。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括AI代理从经验中学习的实际应用范围、奖励机制是否足以实现通用人工智能，以及当前AI技术发展过程中大公司主导模式的潜在风险。
• 讨论还涉及对科学论文缺乏出版日期的实际影响、文章内容的真实性及其是否为公关噱头的质疑。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是知识创造与应用的未来分工，以及模型所有权和开放知识的问题。

43741273.article_content:
The integral of sec(x) is well known to any beginners calculus student. Yet this integral was once a major outstanding maths problem. It was first introduced by Geradus Mercator who needed it to make his famous map in 1569. He couldn’t find it and used an approximation instead. The exact solution was found accidentally 86 years later without calculus in 1645. It then took another two decades until a formal proof was given in 1668, 99 years after Mercator first proposed the problem.
Update 13 March 2021: added a note on how Napier calculated logarithm trigonometry tables. This was prompted by a correction raised in a discussion of this post on
HackerNews
.
Update 10 October 2021: the great circle and rhumb line images are now made with a script that uses
Cartopy
. Previously they were made with a Matlab application. You can see the new script at my
Github repository
and enter your co-ordinates to generate your own lines.
As this
comic
by SMBC rightly teases, the history of mathematics is often not so straightforward.
Theorems, formulas and notation that are routinely discussed in class, were once insights or accidents themselves.
This is the story of one such formula, the integral of the secant.
I first read about it almost a decade ago when I got interested in cartography: the science and art of map making.
1
This integral is of vital importance to the Mercator map and therefore many online maps that use it like
Apple Maps
and
Google Maps
.
This story has been told several times before: see
1
,
2
or
3
.
But these are all journal articles, consigned mostly to academics.
I want to present it here in a less formal and more colourful setting to make it more accessible.
This is an article about mathematics so familiarity with the following is helpful: algebra, trigonometry, radians and basic calculus.
These are usually covered in advanced high school maths classes or first year maths courses.
First year maths
In first year maths at university after a month of differentiation we were starting the inverse problem: integration.
Differentiation  is the mathematics of finding gradient functions for curves.
Integration is the mathematics of inverting this - given a gradient function, what is the curve?
My lecturer was introducing the integration of trigonometric functions.
He started off with:
\[\int \sin(x) dx = -\cos(x) + c \:\text{  and } \int \cos(x) dx = \sin(x) + c\]
This relationship made sense because sine and cosine derivatives were opposites. Just had to be careful of minus signs. Next he derived the integral for the tangent:
\[\int \tan(x) dx = \int \frac{\sin(x)}{\cos(x)}dx = -\ln|\cos(x)| + c\]
Ok, that was tricky. It was not immediately obvious that the inverse of the chain rule could be used here, because the function $\cos(x)$ was present with its derivative $\sin(x)$.
But given enough thought it made sense. Then he said, this is the integral of the secant and learn it off by heart:
\[\int \sec(x) dx = \ln|\sec(x) + \tan(x)| + c\]
OK, where did that come from? My lecturer offered no explanation. It was easy to verify that it worked by finding the derivative.
2
(Paper
2
has a more complex proof using only integration.)
But how had he come up with that?
The curve $\ln|\sec(x) + \tan(x)|$ has tangents with a gradient of $\sec(x)$. Discovering this fact took 100 years.
I think at this point most first year calculus students like me have the following fleeting thoughts:
Integration is much harder than differentiation.
Some mathematician must have stumbled on this through differentiation first.
It doesn’t matter anyway because where will I ever use this?
Actually number 1 is true as many a student can testify after writing a test.
Number 2 is false - in fact it was found by a teacher while looking at raw numbers.
Such a method for finding an integral is so unusual that one might conjecture it is the
only
integral that has been found like this.
Surely in calculus class where raw numbers are so rare you would be laughed at if you attempted to solve an integral like that.
Lastly, number 3 remains true for me. But this doesn’t mean this integral isn’t useful - it is used to construct the Mercator map.
That is why a teacher was crunching numbers when he serendipitously realised what the formula was.
Quick revision: trigonometry
The secant is a standard trigonometric function. It is defined as the ratio of the hypotenuse $c$ to the adjacent side $a$ for an angle $\varphi$ in a right angled triangle.
In mathematical notation the definition is:
\[\sec(\varphi) = \frac{c}{a}\]
It is the reciprocal of the more widely used cosine function:
\[\sec(\varphi) = \frac{1}{\cos(\varphi)}\]
Here are the graphs of the secant and cosine for the angles from $-2\pi$ (-360°) to $2\pi$ (360°):
The integral of the secant can be interpreted as the area under the graph.
3
This is illustrated by the shaded region
An introduction to cartography
The earth cannot be projected onto a flat map without distortion.
Over the years cartographers

data.title: Novel color via stimulation of individual photoreceptors at population scale
data.author: radeeyate
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“不可能的颜色”及其感知方式的讨论

不同观点：
• InsideOutSanta：分享了通过交叉眼睛或高帧率显示器等方法看到“不可能的颜色”的个人经验，包括因激光导致视力受损后看到的奇特颜色。他们认为有些颜色无法通过自然混合得到。
• tianqi：提到许多人从未见过真正的“紫罗兰色”，并通过405nm激光手电筒与朋友体验了单波长紫色的不同。他们还讨论了现代技术能够刺激单个视锥细胞，并认为这种颜色接近#00FFEE。
• foota：对使用高分辨率和高速成像技术来实现细胞刺激的细节感兴趣，并解释了AO-OCT和AO-SLO两种技术的使用。
• ratatoskrt：引用《卫报》文章，提到色彩专家John Barbur的观点，认为这些实验产生的颜色并非新颜色，而是高饱和度的绿色，且实验价值有限。
• robertclaus：提出理论，认为没有命名的颜色难以识别，并质疑100%饱和度的颜色在没有上下文时是否独特。
• mppm：对未来VR技术应用这些技术表示期待，但指出由于光学限制，无法完全隔离单个视锥细胞，从而无法在视网膜上绘制清晰的彩色图像。
• jonas21：质疑实验者在自己和同事身上进行实验的正常性，并怀疑是否因为不愿意对陌生人进行激光刺激实验。
• thenoblesunfish：好奇迷幻药物或其他精神状态改变是否能产生类似的效果，通过内部信号而非外部刺激。
• K0balt：询问“人口规模”在此背景下的意义。
• perihelions：提到另一个关于该论文的讨论线程。
• shermantanktop：作为色盲者，调侃对“正常视力者”争论颜色问题的期待。
• throwanem：联想到科幻小说《Snow Crash》中使用激光在用户视网膜上绘图的技术。
• exe34：幽默地建议将新颜色命名为“octarine”，认为这是科学魔法带来的。

补充讨论：
• foota在后续评论中开玩笑地提到实验可能引发的意外后果，如触发缓冲区溢出，暗示对大脑接收非自然刺激的潜在风险关注。

争议焦点：
• 关于这些“不可能的颜色”是否真正新颖以及其实际应用价值的讨论，例如色彩专家John Barbur对其实验价值的质疑。
• 实验者在自己和同事身上进行激光实验的伦理性和正常性问题。
• 技术上是否能实现对视锥细胞的完全隔离以实现全新颜色体验的实际可行性。

data.title: Pretty State Machine Patterns in Rust (2016)
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了编程中常用的模式和结构，特别是状态机模式。状态机由一组状态和状态之间的转换组成，可以用来模拟各种系统，如TCP连接、HTTP请求或正则表达式等。状态机有助于理解和构建复杂的系统，因为每个状态都有独立的责任和关注点。

文章以一个瓶子灌装机的例子来说明状态机的概念，包括等待、灌装和完成三种状态，以及它们之间的合法转换。状态机模式应在编译时强制执行合法转换，避免无效操作，如从“完成”直接跳到“灌装”。

在Rust中实现状态机时，理想特性包括：一次只能处于一个状态，每个状态有独立的数据，且状态转换应在编译时检查，以确保逻辑正确性。这种模式有助于简化复杂系统的设计和实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中的类型状态模式及状态机的实现与应用

不同观点：
• [phibz] 认为类型状态模式通过将每个状态转移到下一个状态的方法中，可以防止保留对过时状态的访问，从而有效防止错误。此外，使用From trait来实现状态转移可以确保不可能出现不合法的状态转移。这种模式随着时间推移变得越来越常用。
• [gsliepen] 则质疑是否有必要编写显式的状态机，认为普通的、更具可读性的代码（如使用while循环）可以达到同样的效果，且不会减少错误或提高性能。
• [theOGognf] 分享了实际应用经验，指出在实现扑克游戏时使用状态机使开发更安全，并能防止非法状态转移。
• [mijoharas] 指出该方法可能无法处理外部输入的存储问题，即在状态转移时需要存储一个并非从当前状态直接计算得出的外部输入值。

补充讨论：
• [michalsustr] 提到正在开发一个基于rust-fsm crate的库，增加对Mealy自动机的支持，并计划实现将自动机导出到UPPAAL进行模型检查，从而确保模型和实现的一致性。
• [skavi] 建议Rust引入稳定的协程，以便能够用纯命令式代码编写状态机，目前协程仅在async/await中使用，但并未直接暴露。
• [joshka] 更倾向于为状态转移命名，而不是依赖From实现，认为这样可以减少语法噪音和重复，并提供了一个具体的Raft算法示例。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• [nativeit] 对文章中的CSS规则感到好奇，并提出了相关问题。
• [locusofself] 对文章标题是否在向Nine Inch Nails专辑"Pretty Hate Machine"致敬表示好奇。
• [jll29] 提出了关于处理具有数百万次转移的状态机（如字母传感器）的问题。
• [raphinou] 询问是否有推荐的用于开发状态机的crate。
• [pjmlp] 指出这是对Standard ML思想的一种重新发现。
• [jesse__] 认为虽然可以通过泛型节省10行代码，但更喜欢长形式的首次实现。

争议焦点：

43741051.article_content:
Lately I've been thinking a lot about the
patterns
and
structures
which we program with. It's really wonderful to start exploring a project and see familiar patterns and styles which you've already used before. It makes it easier to understand the project, and empowers you to start working on the project faster.
Sometimes you're working on a new project and realize that you need to do something in the same way as you did in another project. This
thing
might not be a functionality or a library, it might not be something which you can encode into some clever macro or small crate. Instead, it may be simply a pattern, or a structural concept which addresses a problem nicely.
One interesting pattern that is commonly applied to problems is that of the 'State Machine'. Let's take some time to consider what exactly we mean when we say that, and why they're interesting.
Throughout this post you can run all examples in
the playground
, I typically use 'Nightly' out of habit.
Founding Our Concepts
There are a
lot
of resources and topical articles about state machines out there on the internet. Even more so, there are a lot of
implementations
of state machines.
Just to get to this web page you used one. You can model TCP as a state machine. You can model HTTP requests with one too. You can model any
regular
language, such as a regex, as a state machine. They're everywhere, hiding inside things we use every day.
So, a State Machine is any
'machine'
which has a set of
'states'
and
'transitions'
defined between them.
When we talk about a machine we're referring to the abstract concept of something which
does something
. For example, your 'Hello World!' function is a machine. It is started and eventually outputs what we expect it to. Some model which you use to interact with your database is just the same. We'll regard our most basic machine simply as a
struct
that can be created and destroyed.
struct
Machine
;
fn
main
(
)
{
let
my_machine
=
Machine
;
//
Create.
//
`my_machine` is destroyed when it falls out of scope below.
}
States are a way to reason about
where
a machine is in its process. For example, we can think about a bottle filling machine as an example. The machine is in a 'waiting' state when it is waiting for a new bottle. Once it detects a bottle it moves to the 'filling' state. Upon detecting the bottle is filled it enters the 'done' state. After the bottle is left the machine we return to the 'waiting' state.
A key takeaway here is that none of the states have any information relevant for the other states. The 'filling' state doesn't care how long the 'waiting' state waited. The 'done' state doesn't care about what rate the bottle was filled at. Each state has
discrete responsibilities and concerns
. The natural way to consider these
variants
is as an
enum
.
enum
BottleFillerState
{
Waiting
{
waiting_time
:
std
::
time
::
Duration
}
,
Filling
{
rate
:
usize
}
,
Done
,
}
struct
BottleFiller
{
state
:
BottleFillerState,
}
Using an
enum
in this way means all the states are mutually exclusive, you can only be in one at a time. Rust's 'fat enums' allow us to have each of these states to carry data with them as well. As far as our current definition is concerned, everything is totally okay.
But there is a bit of a problem here. When we described our bottle filling machine above we described three transitions:
Waiting -> Filling
,
Filling -> Done
, and
Done -> Waiting
. We never described
Waiting -> Done
or
Done -> Filling
, those don't make sense!
This brings us to the idea of transitions. One of the nicest things about a true state machine is we never have to worry about our bottle machine going from
Done -> Filling
, for example. The state machine pattern should
enforce
that this can never happen. Ideally this would be done before we even start running our machine, at compile time.
Let's look again at the transitions we described for our bottle filler in a diagram:
+++++++++++   +++++++++++   ++++++++
|         |   |         |   |      |
| Waiting +-->+ Filling +-->+ Done |
|         |   |         |   |      |
++++-++++-+   +++++++++++   +--+++++
^                         |
+++++++++++++++++++++++++-+
As we can see here there are a finite number of states, and a finite number of transitions between these states. Now, it is possible to have a valid transition between each state and every other state, but in most cases this is not true.
This means moving between a state such as 'Waiting' to a state such as 'Filling' should have defined semantics. In our example this can be defined as "There is a bottle in place." In the case of a TCP stream it might be "We have received a FIN packet" which means we need to finish closing out the stream.
Determining What We Want
Now that we know what a state machine is, how do we represent them in Rust? First, let's think about what we
want
from some pattern.
Ideally, we'd like to see the following characteristics:
Can only be in one state at a time.
Each state should have its own
43741051.article_summary:
本文讨论了编程中常用的模式和结构，特别是状态机模式。状态机由一组状态和状态之间的转换组成，可以用来模拟各种系统，如TCP连接、HTTP请求或正则表达式等。状态机有助于理解和构建复杂的系统，因为每个状态都有独立的责任和关注点。

文章以一个瓶子灌装机的例子来说明状态机的概念，包括等待、灌装和完成三种状态，以及它们之间的合法转换。状态机模式应在编译时强制执行合法转换，避免无效操作，如从“完成”直接跳到“灌装”。

在Rust中实现状态机时，理想特性包括：一次只能处于一个状态，每个状态有独立的数据，且状态转换应在编译时检查，以确保逻辑正确性。这种模式有助于简化复杂系统的设计和实现。

data.title: Layered Design in Go
data.author: misonic
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Go语言中设计程序的分层方法。Go的包不允许循环引用，这是设计中的一个关键约束。作者反对将所有代码放入单个包的做法，因为这会丧失信息隐藏的优势。作者的分层设计通过将包按依赖关系从下至上排列，形成一个有向无环图（DAG）。底层包提供基础功能，如日志、指标等，上层包依赖底层包实现更高级的功能。这种分层是描述性的，而非规定性的，任何Go程序的设计都必须遵循这种结构。作者不认同一些文章中关于层级严格限制的观点，认为包可以跨多层引用。这种分层设计为Go程序提供了一种系统化的组织方式。

Page content
This post will describe how I design my programs in Go. I needed this
for work, and while I searched for a link, nothing
quite
fits my
coding practices out there. The word “Layered” can pull up some fairly
close descriptions, but I want to lay out what I do.
Deriving Some Requirements
Go has a rule that I believe is underappreciated in its utility and
whose implications are often not fully grasped, which is: Packages may
not circularly reference each other. It is strictly forbidden. A
compile error.
Packages are also the primary way of hiding information within Go,
through the mechanism of
exported and unexported fields and
identifiers in the package
. Some people
will pile everything into a single package, and while I’m not quite
ready to call this unconditionally a bad idea, it does involve
sacrificing all ability to use information hiding to maintain
invariants, and that is a heck of a tool to put down. At any sort of
scale, you’d better have some concept of the discipline you’re going
to replace that with.
So for the purposes of this discussion, I’m going to discard the
“one large package approach”.
We also know that Go uses a package named
main
that contains a
function named
main
to define the entry point for a given
executable. The resulting package import structure is a
directed acyclic
graph
, where
the packages are the nodes and the imports are the directed edges, and
there is a distinguished “top node” for each executable.
So how do I deal with this requirement in Go?
Layered Design In Go
This is a portion of a package hierarchy extracted from a real
project, with many of the names substituted and rubbed off, but the
relationships are approximately correct:
A sample set of packages
All imports of external modules are automatically not part of a loop
in the base package, so we can just look at the import patterns of the
application currently being written. Since loops are forbidden that
implies there must be packages that do not import any other package in
the application. Pull those out and put them on the bottom:
The packages that reference nothing separated.
There is now a set of packages in the remaining set that only
reference the packages we just pulled out and put on the bottom. Put
them in their own layer:
The packages that reference only the lower layer sorted out.
You can repeat this process until you’ve layered everything by the
depth of the import stack:
The layers.
All package imports now point downwards, though it can be hard to
tell.
If you look at the bottom, you see very basic things, like
“the package that provides metrics to everything else”,
“the package that refines the logging for our system”, and
“a set data structure”.
These are composed up into slightly higher level functionality that
uses logging, metrics, etc. and puts together things like header
functionality, or information about users (imagine permissions or
metadata are stored here).
Throughout this post I will refer “higher level packages”; in this
case, it literally refers to the way packages will appear “higher” on
this graph than any package it imports. It is not the definition of
“higher” we often use to mean “higher level of abstraction”; yes,
if a package offers a “higher level of abstraction” it will generally
of necessity also be a “higher level package”, but a
“higher level package” is often just a package that is using the lower
level package, not an abstraction, e.g., a “crawler” may have
net/http
show up as a “lower level package” but a crawler is not any
sort of abstraction around
net/http
so much as it is just an
application that is using
net/http
.
These things are then composed into higher layer objects, and so
forth, and so forth, until you finally get to the desired application
functionality.
This Is Descriptive, Not Prescriptive
If you are the sort of person who reads things about software
architecture, you are used to people making prescriptive statements
about design. For instance, one such statement I found in another
article about layered design in Go has the prescriptive statement that
layers should be organized into very formal layers, and that no layer
should ever reach down more than one level to import a package. That
is not a requirement imposed by Go, it is a
prescriptive
statement
by the author. You can see in my graph above I don’t agree with that
particular prescription, as I have imports that reach down multiple
levels.
However, the previous section is not prescriptive. It may sound like
prescriptions you’ve heard before, but it’s actually
required
. You
can graph
all
Go modules in the layers I described. It’s a
mathematical consequence of the rules for how packages are allowed to
import each other. It is descriptive of the reality in Go.
Which means that any other prescriptive design for a Go program
must
sit on top of this structure. It has no choice. It may not be
necessary, but it is certainly
convenient
in MVC design for the
Model, View, and Controller to be able to

data.title: Eccfrog512ck2: An Enhanced 512-Bit Weierstrass Elliptic Curve [pdf]
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新的椭圆曲线"Eccfrog512ck2"，它基于512位Weierstrass形式，提供了256位安全强度，并在性能上优于NIST P-521曲线。该曲线具有侧信道攻击抵抗能力，并避免了如MOV攻击等弱点。实验显示，Eccfrog512ck2在标量乘法上速度提升61.5%，在点生成上速度提升33.3%。该曲线适用于需要高安全性和高性能的密钥交换和数字签名应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新提出的曲线参数选择及其透明性和可信度

不同观点：
• Retr0id认为，文章中对系数b如何通过BLAKE3确定缺乏详细说明，同时对素数模数的选择过程也没有具体阐述，只是列举了其有利属性。Retr0id建议分享选择素数模数的具体代码或过程，以增加透明度。
  
• kevvok从行业趋势的角度提出质疑，认为在当前向post-quantum算法转变的背景下，新的椭圆曲线可能不会获得太多关注，暗示该技术可能缺乏长期应用前景。

• commandersaki质疑为何选择该曲线而不是已经存在的Curve448和Ed448，并询问该曲线是否在实现上更简单。这表明对新曲线是否具有显著优势存在疑问。

• quesomaster9000对曲线参数和文档的可信度提出强烈质疑，指出以下问题：
  - 生成器不是通过确定性方法选择的；
  - OpenFrogget代码中的BLAKE3(seed)结果与Python和Javascript的实现不匹配；
  - 文章中未具体说明索引和种子；
  - 对选择`a=-7`的原因缺乏解释；
  - 参考实现和论文中的参数不一致。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于曲线参数的透明性和可重现性，尤其是关于BLAKE3的使用和生成器的选择。quesomaster9000特别指出其实验结果与文档不符，质疑该方案的可信度。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是新曲线与现有曲线（如Curve448和Ed448）的比较，commandersaki认为需要明确新曲线的优势才能被广泛接受。

Abstract:
Whilst many key exchange and digital signature methods use the NIST P256 (secp256r1) and secp256k1 curves, there is often a demand for increased security. With these curves, we have a 128-bit security. These security levels can be increased to 256-bit security with NIST P-521 Curve 448 and Brainpool-P512. This paper outlines a new curve - Eccfrog512ck2 - and which provides 256-bit security and enhanced performance over NIST P-521. Along with this, it has side-channel resistance and is designed to avoid weaknesses such as related to the MOV attack. It shows that Eccfrog512ck2 can have a 61.5% speed-up on scalar multiplication and a 33.3% speed-up on point generation over the NIST P-521 curve.

43708789.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新的椭圆曲线"Eccfrog512ck2"，它基于512位Weierstrass形式，提供了256位安全强度，并在性能上优于NIST P-521曲线。该曲线具有侧信道攻击抵抗能力，并避免了如MOV攻击等弱点。实验显示，Eccfrog512ck2在标量乘法上速度提升61.5%，在点生成上速度提升33.3%。该曲线适用于需要高安全性和高性能的密钥交换和数字签名应用。
43708789.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新提出的曲线参数选择及其透明性和可信度

不同观点：
• Retr0id认为，文章中对系数b如何通过BLAKE3确定缺乏详细说明，同时对素数模数的选择过程也没有具体阐述，只是列举了其有利属性。Retr0id建议分享选择素数模数的具体代码或过程，以增加透明度。
  
• kevvok从行业趋势的角度提出质疑，认为在当前向post-quantum算法转变的背景下，新的椭圆曲线可能不会获得太多关注，暗示该技术可能缺乏长期应用前景。

• commandersaki质疑为何选择该曲线而不是已经存在的Curve448和Ed448，并询问该曲线是否在实现上更简单。这表明对新曲线是否具有显著优势存在疑问。

• quesomaster9000对曲线参数和文档的可信度提出强烈质疑，指出以下问题：

data.title: If you use AI to write me that note, don't expect me to read it
data.author: gortok
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI生成内容的看法与使用是否合适

不同观点：
• **认为AI生成内容不尊重时间和精力**：
  - [lurk2] 认为AI生成的消息缺乏思考和时间投入，阅读这些内容比生成它们需要更多的时间和精力，这是一种不尊重。
  - [DrSiemer] 指出批评AI生成内容的人通常是那些能够轻易辨别出AI生成内容的人，但许多人缺乏时间和写作能力，对他们来说，AI生成内容是一种升级。

• **对AI生成内容的厌倦和反应**：
  - [morsecodist] 认为如果双方都使用AI生成和总结内容，整个交流过程变得多余和荒谬。
  - [willquack] 提到因为人们厌倦了低质量的AI生成内容，现在看起来像是AI生成的文本常常被 dismiss 或看低。为了避免这种情况，他开始故意引入小的拼写或语法错误，并避免使用典型的AI写作特征。

• **对AI生成内容的接受与合理使用**：
  - [thunky] 通过类比指出，人们在不同情境下对投入时间和精力的期望不同，不能总是取悦所有人。
  - [yellowapple] 认为使用AI生成内容就像在聚会上带一份微波炉晚餐，只要其他人也这么做，就没有什么可尴尬的。

• **幽默与讽刺**：
  - [corobo] 提出了一种新的讽刺性缩写 "tf;drTuring (test) failed; didn't read"，用来表达对AI生成内容的抵制。
  - [gblargg] 以幽默的方式建议使用AI生成冗长且明显是AI生成的回复。

• **对AI生成内容真实性的怀疑**：
  - [kcatskcolbdi] 对某些声称通过AI生成交到聪明朋友的说法表示怀疑，认为需要更多的证据支持。

• **完全接受AI的使用**：
  - [antman] 表示已经完全接受使用AI来阅读文章，没有问题。

补充讨论：
• **关于AI生成内容礼仪的争议**：
  - [kstenerud] 反驳认为要求手动写公式化信件是不合理的，使用AI来总结是更有效的方式，并将这种反对意见视为一种无礼的要求。

争议焦点：
• AI生成内容是否是不尊重时间和精力的表现，以及在不同情境下使用AI生成内容的合理性和接受度。

data.title: Smart People Can Stop Being Miserable
data.author: handfuloflight
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了智力和幸福之间的关系，指出聪明人不一定更幸福。研究显示，总体智力与生活满意度之间没有直接关联，只有在空间视觉化、记忆力和处理速度方面有短暂关联。此外，词汇量大的人反而可能因为选择更具挑战的环境而面临更多压力，导致幸福感降低。文章强调，智力和幸福的关系取决于如何使用智力：若用于追求金钱、权力、享乐和声望，可能不会带来幸福；若用于服务他人，则更可能获得幸福。最终，作者建议将智力视为资源，通过分享和行善来提升幸福感。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于智力、幸福感以及人际关系的讨论，涉及影视剧《House》中的一集以及对一篇有关聪明人与幸福关系文章的评论。

不同观点：
• [benoau的观点] 通过《House》中的一集"Ignorance is Bliss"探讨聪明人与工作、人际关系的复杂性。Sidas为了与妻子Dara建立更好的关系，选择降低自己的智力以减少对她的伤害。同时，这与House角色自身的困境相似，House依赖工作带来的满足感，但智力却阻碍了他与他人建立深层次的关系。

• [hn_user82179的观点] 对文章内容持怀疑态度，认为文章讨论的内容容易让读者陷入邓宁-克鲁格效应，即高估自己的智力。尤其对文章中建议聪明人分享想法和不要贬低他人的观点表示质疑，认为这些建议并非仅与智力相关，更多是性格和自我价值问题。此外，对文章中提到的词汇量与幸福感的关系提出不同看法，认为可能有其他因素如生活方式或职业特性影响幸福感。

• [stormfather的观点] 提出通过寻求精神或宗教上的帮助（如祈求圣灵）可能对解决智力与幸福之间的矛盾有帮助，虽然不确定是否为安慰剂效应，但值得一试。

• [snvzz的观点] 以讽刺口吻评论，认为变得“愚蠢”可能会更容易获得幸福，暗示智力可能与幸福感负相关，但明显是玩笑语气，不鼓励真正采取这种做法。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于智力是否必然导致不幸福，以及聪明人是否应该通过改变自己（如降低智力或改变行为方式）来获得更好的人际关系和幸福感。
• hn_user82179对文章中提到的“百万美元想法”是否存在被囤积的可能性表示怀疑，认为分享成功秘诀与智力并无直接关联。
• 不同观点中对智力与幸福关系的理解存在明显分歧，部分认为智力是障碍，部分则认为文章的解释不充分或有误。

“
How to Build a Life
”
is a column by Arthur Brooks, tackling questions of meaning and happiness.
Click here
to listen to his podcast series on all things happiness,
How to Build a Happy Life
.
“H
appiness in intelligent people
is the rarest thing I know,” an unnamed character casually
remarks
in Ernest Hemingway’s novel
The Garden of Eden
. You might say that this is a corollary of the much more famous “Ignorance is bliss.”
The latter recalls phenomena such as the
Dunning-Kruger effect
—in which people lacking skills and knowledge in a particular area innocently underestimate their own incompetence—and the
illusion of explanatory depth
, which can prompt autodidacts on social media to excitedly present complex scientific phenomena, thinking they understand them in far greater depth than they really do.
The Hemingway hypothesis, however, is less straightforward. I can think of a lot of
unhappy intellectuals
, to be sure. But is intelligence per se their problem? Happiness scholars have studied this question, and the answer is—as in so many parts of life—
it depends
. The gifts you possess can lift you up or pull you down; it all depends on how you use them. Many people see intelligence as a way to get ahead of others. But to get happier, we need to do the opposite.
Y
ou might assume
that intelligence—whether it be the conventional IQ kind,
emotional intelligence
, musical talent, or some other dimension along which a person can excel—raises happiness, all else being equal. After all, people with higher cognitive ability should logically have more exciting life opportunities than others. They should also acquire more resources with which to enhance their well-being.
In general, however, there is
no correlation
between general intelligence and life satisfaction at the individual level. That principle does mask a few wrinkles. In 2022, researchers at Weill Cornell Medicine and Fordham University
looked
at the association between well-being and various building blocks of neurocognitive ability: memory, processing speed, reasoning, spatial visualization, and vocabulary. The only components of intelligence that they found to be positively related to happiness were spatial visualization, memory, and processing speed—but those relationships were fleeting and age-related.
Read: Why so many smart people aren’t happy
More interesting, the researchers also found a strongly
negative
association between happiness and vocabulary. To explain this, they offered a hypothesis: People with a large vocabulary “self-select more challenging environments, and as a result may encounter more daily stressors and reduced positive affect.” In other words, loquacious logophiles might have byzantine lives and find themselves in manifold precarious situations that lower their jouissance. (They talk themselves into misery.)
The whole intelligence-and-happiness question needs more research, which I suspect it will receive in the coming years. But I think there is a clear reason that something as valuable as intelligence, especially manifested in one’s ability to communicate, doesn’t necessarily lead to a higher quality of life.
One of life’s cruelest mysteries is why we are impelled to pursue rewards that bring success, but not happiness. Mother Nature drives us toward the four goals of
money, power, pleasure, and prestige
with the promise that these rewards will bring happiness. In truth, the
correlation
might be positive, but the
causation
is probably reversed: Happier people naturally get these rewards. But seek them for their own sake, for your own gain, and happiness will likely
fall
. Accordingly, if you aspire to use your cleverness for personal benefit—for the praise and admiration of others, or an advantage in work and dating—woe be unto you.
From the March 2022 issue: How to want less
The smarter you are, the better equipped you should be to understand that well-being comes from
faith, family, friendship, and work that serves others
. Your intelligence is more likely to bring you happiness if you put it to use by chasing better ways to love and serve others, rather than elbowing others aside and hoarding worldly rewards.
I
n some ways,
you can think of intelligence as a resource just like money or power. We know how to make the latter two
sources of joy
: Share them with others, and use them as a force for good in the world. To make smarts a fount of happiness, too, we can follow the same guide. Here are a couple of tangible proposals.
1. Give your ideas away.
It amazes me how many pious philanthropists give generously to charity but are loath to share the secrets of their success. In a world powered by ideas, keeping good ones to yourse

主要讨论点：STEM与花样滑冰结合的活动及其可行性和具体实现

不同观点：
• [svisa] 介绍了一个由科技从业者发起的活动和组织（SVISA），其目的是通过结合STEM和花样滑冰来保护本地的冰场。他们举办了一个名为"STEM Ice"的活动，旨在将科技与花样滑冰结合起来，并提供了更多信息的链接和加入他们邮件列表的邀请。

data.title: Let's give PRO/VENIX a barely adequate, pre-C89 TCP/IP stack, featuring Slirp-CK
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讲述了作者多年前计划为Commodore 64编写TCP/IP协议栈，但未付诸实践。与此同时，其他人成功实现了这一目标。作者曾购买了《TCP/IP Illustrated》套装，但至今未拆封。文章主要内容是关于作者最近在一个不支持网络的DEC Professional 380系统上（运行基于System V的PRO/VENIX V2.0）成功实现了一个简易的网络栈，并通过SLIP和Crypto Ancienne代理下载了Google主页。

文章还回顾了DEC早期个人电脑的历史，尤其是DEC Professional系列因市场策略而与PDP-11系列不完全兼容的情况。DEC Professional最终获得了基于V7和System V Release 2.0的Unix系统PRO/VENIX。作者提到，DEC曾尝试将Ultrix-11移植到该系统，但因性能问题而放弃，转而采用VenturCom的Venix。文章包含了详细的源代码和实现方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在复古计算机上实现TCP/IP栈及相关网络功能的尝试和挑战

不同观点：
• [trollbridge] 分享了自己在PC BASIC环境下实现SLIP和TCP/IP栈的经历。他指出该项目面临的多个技术挑战，包括在9,600波特率以上时字符丢失的问题、计算校验和的复杂性、64K内存限制以及调用外部编辑器时连接中断的问题。尽管如此，他的项目最终还是成功运行了。

• [jrdres] 提到目前有一种趋势，即在复古机器上从头实现TCP/IP功能。他引用了M Brutman的"mTCP"驱动程序以及DogCow在128K Macintosh上开发的"Sabina"网络套件，指出这些项目尽管进展缓慢，但显示了对复古计算机网络功能的持续兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [pjmlp] 简短评论，认为这是一个有趣的历史片段，认可了这些技术探索的历史价值。

争议焦点：
• 实现这些技术在现代看来是否有实际意义存在争议。一方面，[trollbridge]的项目展示了技术上的可行性，但其面临的诸多限制和挑战也表明在大规模应用上的困难。另一方面，[jrdres]提到的趋势显示了社区对这些复古技术探索的持续兴趣。

• 不同项目进展缓慢的原因可能包括技术难度、时间限制以及社区资源的有限性。这些因素共同影响着复古计算机网络功能的开发和实现。

43741849.article_content:
I had this grand idea many moons ago about writing up a TCP/IP stack for the Commodore 64, along with a lot of other people, and several of those people eventually did so before I even wrote a single opcode of 6502 assembly. For that purpose I had bought the box set of
TCP/IP Illustrated
(what would now be called the first edition prior to the 2011 update) for a hundred-odd bucks on sale which has now sat on my bookshelf, encased in its original shrinkwrap, for at least twenty years. It would be fun to put up the 4.4BSD data structures poster it came with but that would require opening it.
Fortunately, today
we have AI
we have many more excellent and comprehensive documents on the subject, and more importantly, we've recently brought back up an oddball platform that doesn't have networking either: our DEC Professional 380 running the System V-based PRO/VENIX V2.0, which you met
a couple articles back
. The DEC Professionals are a notoriously incompatible member of the PDP-11 family and, short of DECnet (DECNA) support in its unique Professional Operating System, there's officially no other way you can get one on a network — let alone the modern Internet. Are we going to let that stop us?
Of course not! Here's our barebones network stack for PRO/VENIX, the Pro's only official Unix option, downloading the Google home page on real hardware (internal addresses bleeped out) over SLIP and a
Crypto Ancienne
proxy for TLS 1.3. And, as we'll discuss, if you can get
this
thing on the network, you can get almost
anything
on the network! Easily portable and painfully verbose source code is included.
Recall from our lengthy history of
DEC's early misadventures with personal computers
that, in Digital's ill-advised plan to avoid the DEC Pros cannibalizing low-end sales from their categorical PDP-11 minicomputers, Digital's Small Systems Group deliberately made the DEC Professional series nearly totally incompatible despite the fact they used the same CPUs. In their initial roll-out strategy in 1982, the Pros (as well as their sibling systems, the Rainbow and the DECmate II) were only supposed to be mere desktop office computers — the fact the Pros were PDP-11s internally was mostly treated as an implementation detail. The idea backfired spectacularly against the IBM PC when the Pros and their promised office software failed to arrive on time and in 1984 DEC retooled around a new concept of explicitly selling the Pros as desktop PDP-11s. This required porting operating systems that PDP-11 minis typically ran: RSX-11M Plus was already there as the low-level layer of the Professional Operating System (P/OS), and DEC internally ported RT-11 (as PRO/RT-11) and COS.
PDP-11s were also famous for running Unix and so DEC needed a Unix for the Pro as well, though eventually only one official option was ever available: a port of VenturCom's Venix based on V7 Unix and later System V Release 2.0 called PRO/VENIX. After the
last article
, I had the distinct pleasure of being contacted by Paul Kleppner, the company's first paid employee in 1981, who was part of the group at VenturCom that did the Pro port and stayed at the company until 1988. Venix was originally developed from V6 Unix on the PDP-11/23 incorporating Myron Zimmerman's real-time extensions to the kernel (such as semaphores and asynchronous I/O), then a postdoc in physics at MIT; Kleppner's father was the professor of the lab Zimmerman worked in. Zimmerman founded VenturCom in 1981 to capitalize on the emerging Unix market, becoming one of the earliest commercial Unix licensees. Venix-11 was subsequently based on the later V7 Unix, as was Venix/86, which was the first Unix on the IBM PC in January 1983 and was ported to the DEC Rainbow as Venix/86R. In addition to its real-time extensions and enhanced segmentation capability, critical for memory management in smaller 16-bit address spaces, it also included a full desktop graphics package.
Notably, DEC themselves were also a Unix licensee through their Unix Engineering Group and already had an enhanced V7 Unix of their own running on the PDP-11, branded initially as V7M. Subsequently the UEG developed a port of 4.2BSD with some System V components for the VAX and planned to release it as Ultrix-32, simultaneously retconning V7M as Ultrix-11 even though it had little in common with the VAX release. Paul recalls that DEC did attempt a port of Ultrix-11 to the Pro 350 themselves but ran into intractable performance problems. By then the clock was ticking on the Pro relaunch and the issues with Ultrix-11 likely prompted DEC to look for alternatives. Crucially, Zimmerman had managed to upgrade Venix-11's kernel while still keeping it small, a vital aspect on his 11/23 which lacked split instruction and data addressing and would have had to page in and out a larger kernel otherwise. data.title: Attention Spans for Math and Stories (2019)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过故事激发儿童对数学的兴趣，尤其是对年幼儿童而言。文章提到在一个MathOverflow讨论中，人们探讨了适合5-6岁儿童的数学游戏，强调了成年人往往低估5岁儿童的理解能力。对于年幼的孩子，抽象逻辑游戏的吸引力在于提出核心玩法之外的问题，比如Set游戏中的特殊技巧，但这些通常要到7-8岁后才会引发兴趣。文章指出，通过故事引导孩子学习数学概念非常有效，例如通过《The Boy Who Loved Math》这本书，作者成功地让一个5岁的小女孩Anna对质数产生了兴趣，尽管她之前对数学并无特别关注。作者还分享了自己作为夏令营辅导员通过编造秘密特工训练故事吸引孩子们注意力的经验，强调了故事讲述在教育中的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过故事和情境帮助理解数学和设计

不同观点：
• vonnik: 认为建筑和设计中的每个物体都蕴含着一个故事，这些故事不仅体现在物体内部各部分的关系上，还体现在这些部分与外部世界（如使用者）的关系上。通过观察六岁孩子用乐高积木构建并解释每个部分的功能，他意识到设计的本质就是在讲故事，且这些故事会随着人们的需求和期望改变而变化。

• aoki: 主张在基础数学和本科数学之间需要更多以故事为导向的内容，类似于YouTube频道Numberphile中的某些节目。建议通过故事引入更深的理论，同时保持趣味性，并提到Beast Academy漫画系列是一个不错的儿童数学启蒙资源。

• AudiomaticApp: 提起Murderous Maths（一本以故事形式讲解数学的书），可能是在回应aoki的观点，暗示这类书籍可以作为数学教育的补充材料。

• ho_schi: 对通过故事来进行数学教育的方法表示赞同，但带有个人感慨，认为这种方法在自身童年时未被采用，是一种遗憾。

• wslh: 分享了Raymond Smullyan的书中提到的故事，强调通过故事激发逻辑和数学兴趣的有效性，并提到一个孩子虽然喜欢解谜却不被告知这是数学，因为他讨厌数学，这暗示了故事在克服对数学反感方面的潜在作用。

• sinenomine: 从遗传学和统计学角度提出不同观点，认为数学能力和智力的遗传性导致天才数学家的孩子往往不如父母，并认为早期教育计划难以弥补这种差距。这与其他人强调教育方法的观点形成对比。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个具体资源和例子，如John Collison的推文、Numberphile、Beast Academy、Murderous Maths和Raymond Smullyan的书，这些都被视为通过故事促进数学理解的有效工具。
• sinenomine的观点引发了对天赋和遗传限制的讨论，与其他评论中强调教育方法的乐观态度形成对比，成为争议的焦点。
• 总体而言，讨论围绕如何通过故事和情境更好地理解和教授数学和设计，但也有对个体差异和遗传因素的现实考虑。

43709843.article_content:
Attention spans for math and stories
#essays
2024-11-15
Editor’s note
: This essay was originally published in 2019.
I have made minor edits in this republishing.
There was a
MathOverflow
thread
about mathematically interesting games for 5–6 year olds. A lot of the
discussion revolved around how young age 5 really is, and how we should temper
expectations because we don’t really remember what it’s like to be 5. In
response to an
enormous answer
by
Alexander Chervov, user LSpice quipped, “‘Daddy, daddy, let’s play another in
the infinite indexed family of perfect-information draw-free cheap-to-construct
two-player games!’” That being said,
Martín-Blas Pérez Pinilla’s “sprouts”
game
piqued my interest to find
optimal strategies.
Most abstract logic games that are interesting to mathy folks are only
interesting when you start asking questions beyond core gameplay. For example,
the game
Set
is interesting when you ask, “how
many cards can you have with no set?” or similar
tricks to determine the last
un-dealt card
in a
deck just by viewing the remaining board. These have little to do with skill at
playing the game.
I’ve found that children under a certain age,
maybe 7 or 8,
haven’t learned how to be curious about such questions yet.
They like
knowing
things and
experiencing
things.
They enjoy surprising patterns
or natural phenomena (like vinegar and baking soda),
but still aren’t really
curious
enough about them to
be persistent in studying them.
For children to exercise mathematical reasoning skills, and for teachers and
parents to get the opportunity to teach curiousity and persistence, they have
to be motivated. People with an eye for science, people who in their adulthood
marvel at the splendor of nature, often neglect that at age 5, there is one
simple thing that kids embrace with all their being, justification-free, which
can be used as a vessel for abstract reasoning: storytelling. Be good at
storytelling.
A few years ago, my cousin’s daughter was 5 years old. I’ll refer to her as
Anna. Anna is of Hungarian descent, lives in Germany, and speaks functional
English. My cousin knew her daughter was bright, but she was at a loss for what
to give Anna to occupy her mind. So naturally I sent my cousin the book, “
The
Boy Who Loved
Math
.”
Cover of
The Boy Who Loved Math
It’s a story about Paul Erdős, the famous Hungarian mathematician. The book is
in English, about a Hungarian boy, and involves a strict German nanny.
Naturally, Anna loved the book because she had someone to identify with her
multiplex identity.
At its most mathematical, “The Boy Who Loved Math” explains what a prime number
is, and Anna learned it immediately. My cousin told me about how one day they
were listening to the radio in the car, and a game show was playing where the
prize-winning question was (I paraphrase), “What is the name for a number that
has only itself and 1 as a factor?” The contestant on the radio couldn’t
answer, but Anna pipes up, “That’s easy, it’s a prime!” To the best of my
knowledge, she had no interest in math before this, and she had no use for
knowing what a prime number is. But simply having the idea
of a prime number wrapped up in a story about someone like her was enough to
pique her interest.
This story has nothing to do with math, but has a lot to do with storytelling.
I worked as a day camp counselor for a few summers in high school and college.
My main age group was 5-6 year old boys and girls. It’s a lovely age group
because they’re old enough to understand complex ideas, but too young to
directly challenge you when you lie to them. And I lied like the wind.
My shtick was to tell the kids that the summer camp was a secret agent training
camp. All the counselors were former secret agents that had retired and were
now training the next generation. By the end of each 3-week session, most of
the kids figured out that it was make-believe, but it was
fun
make-believe
and there was just enough to keep it plausible.
The crown jewel of this act was that it was an infinite time sink. Often
enough, our schedule had us playing an hour of field hockey followed by an hour
of tennis in 95 degree heat (even in normal weather, a 6 year old won’t have
more than 15 minutes of tennis in them before they get bored or frustrated by a
lack of hand-eye coordination). On such hot days, I would end the activities
early and have the kids gather around in the shade to regale them with a tale
about a “mission” another counselor and I had embarked on in our long, storied
career.
The formula was pretty simple:
Pick an evil boss: Doctor Euler.
Choose an exotic locale for a base: inside an iceberg.
Pick an “element” (sand, grass, dirt, mud) for the evil boss’s henchmen to
be built out of (so that we can “kill” them without resorting to gratuitous
violence; guns don’t work on grass monsters).
As you can tell from the name of the evil boss, I liked to slip in math names
for things. Turns out, mathematicians have terrifying and authentic name

• wslh: 分享了Raymond Smullyan的书中提到的故事，强调通过故事激发逻辑和数学兴趣的有效性，并提到一个孩子虽然喜欢解谜却不被告知这是数学，因为他讨厌数学，这暗示了故事在克服对数学反感方面的潜在作用。

• sinenomine: 从遗传学和统计学角度提出不同观点，认为数学能力和智力的遗传性导致天才数学家的孩子往往不如父母，并认为早期教育计划难以弥补这种差距。这与其他人强调教育方法的观点形成对比。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个具体资源和例子，如John Collison的推文、Numberphile、Beast Academy、Murderous Maths和Raymond Smullyan的书，这些都被视为通过故事促进数学理解的有效工具。
• sinenomine的观点引发了对天赋和遗传限制的讨论，与其他评论中强调教育方法的乐观态度形成对比，成为争议的焦点。
• 总体而言，讨论围绕如何通过故事和情境更好地理解和教授数学和设计，但也有对个体差异和遗传因素的现实考虑。

data.title: Police algorithm said Lina was at 'medium' risk. Then she was killed
data.author: mmarian
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了西班牙一名叫Lina的女性在其前伴侣的暴力威胁下，尽管向警方求助并被录入VioGén系统评估为“中等”风险，但仍未获得足够保护，最终被前伴侣杀害的悲剧。VioGén是西班牙警方使用的一种算法工具，用于评估家暴受害者再次遭受攻击的风险，并据此分配警力资源。Lina曾请求法院对其前伴侣下达限制令，但被拒绝。她的死亡引发了对VioGén系统有效性的质疑，尤其是中等风险级别的受害者未能得到及时保护。批评者认为，警方过度依赖算法决策，可能忽略了人的判断。尽管警方认为VioGén总体有效，但Lina的案例表明该系统并非万无一失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：算法责任与事故责任归属的争论

不同观点：
• SOLAR_FIELDS认为，算法本身不应被指责，真正应该负责的是设计和实现算法的个人或组织。他强调，新闻标题不应将责任归咎于模糊的“算法”，而应明确指出是“由X编写并由Y部署的警察软件导致了死亡”。他将责任归结于具体的人为因素，而不是技术本身。

• LatteLazy则从风险评估的角度出发，认为算法所做的只是统计学上的风险预测，类似于购买彩票的中奖概率。尽管有人可能会因为“中等风险”而遭遇不幸，但这只是统计结果与现实的交汇，而非系统性的错误或人为过失。

• rayiner的观点集中在文章中对事件描述的被动语态上。他强烈反对将事件描述为由抽象的“算法”导致的，并指出这是对责任的模糊化处理。他明确指出，真正导致悲剧发生的是人的行为（例如某人故意纵火），而不是技术本身。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于责任归属问题。SOLAR_FIELDS和rayiner都强调个人或组织的责任，而LatteLazy则试图从统计学和风险管理的角度来解释事件，认为这是概率问题，而非直接的人为错误。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对语言和叙述方式的关注，尤其是rayiner对被动语态的批评，认为这种叙述模糊了真正的责任人。
- 三种观点都试图将责任从“算法”这个抽象概念转移到具体的人或机制上，显示出对技术中立性的不同理解。

Image source,
Family handout
Image caption,
Lina died at her home on 9th February, 2025
Linda Pressly and Esperanza Escribano
BBC News
Published
19 April 2025
In January, Lina went to the police.
Her ex-partner had been threatening her at home in the Spanish seaside town of BenalmÃ¡dena. That day, he'd allegedly raised his hand as if to hit her.
"There had been violent episodes - she was scared," Lina's cousin Daniel recalls.
When she got to the police station, she was interviewed and her case registered with VioGÃ©n, a digital tool which assesses the likelihood of a woman being attacked again by the same man.
VioGÃ©n - an algorithm-based system - asks 35 questions about the abuse and its intensity, the aggressor's access to weapons, his mental health and whether the woman has left, or is considering leaving, the relationship.
It then records the threat to her as "negligible", "low", "medium", "high" or "extreme".
The category is used to make decisions about the allocation of police resources to protect the woman.
Lina was deemed to be at "medium" risk.
She asked for a restraining order at a specialist gender violence court in Malaga, so that her ex-partner couldn't be in contact with her or share her living space.  The request was denied.
Can an algorithm predict murder?
Spanish police use an algorithm to assess the risk of repeat domestic violence.  Does it work?
Listen on Sounds
"Lina wanted to change the locks at her home, so she could live peacefully with her children," says her cousin.
Three weeks later, she was dead. Her partner had allegedly used his key to enter her flat and soon the house was on fire.
While her children, mother and ex-partner all escaped, Lina didn't. Her 11-year-old son was widely reported as telling police it was his father who killed his mother.
Lina's lifeless body was retrieved from the charred interior of her home. Her ex-partner, the father of her three youngest children, was arrested.
Now, her death is raising questions about VioGÃ©n and its ability to keep women safe in Spain.
Image caption,
Lina's home after the fire
VioGÃ©n didn't accurately predict the threat to Lina.
As a woman designated at "medium" risk, the protocol is that she would be followed up again by a nominated police officer within 30 days.
But Lina was dead before that. If she had been "high" risk, the police follow-up would have happened within a week.  Could that have made a difference to Lina?
Tools to evaluate the threat of repeat domestic violence are used in North America and across Europe. In the UK, some police forces use DARA (Domestic Abuse Risk Assessment) - essentially a checklist. And DASH (Domestic Abuse, Stalking, Harassment and Honour-based Violence Assessment) may be employed by police or others, like social workers, to assess the risk of another attack.
But only in Spain is an algorithm woven so tightly into police practice. VioGÃ©n was developed by Spanish police and academics.  It's used everywhere apart from the Basque Country and Catalonia (those regions have separate systems, although police co-operation is nationwide).
Image caption,
Ch Insp Isabel Espejo believes VioGÃ©n is an invaluable tool
The head of the National Police's family and women's unit in Malaga, Ch Insp Isabel Espejo, describes VioGÃ©n as "super-important".
"It helps us follow each victim's case very precisely," she says.
Her officers deal with an average of 10 reports of gender violence a day. And every month, VioGÃ©n classifies nine or 10 women as being at "extreme" risk of repeat victimisation.
The resource implications in those cases are huge: 24-hour police protection for a woman until the circumstances change and the risk decreases. Women assessed as "high" risk may also get an officer escort.
A 2014 study found that officers accepted VioGÃ©n's evaluation of the likelihood of repeated abuse 95% of the time. Critics suggest police are abdicating decision-making about women's safety to an algorithm.
Ch Insp Espejo says that the algorithm's calculation of risk is usually adequate. But she recognises  - even though Lina's case wasn't under her command - that something went wrong with Lina's assessment.
"I'm not going to say VioGÃ©n doesn't fail â it does. But this wasn't the trigger that led to this woman's murder. The only guilty party is the person who killed Lina. Total security just doesn't exist," she says.
But at "medium" risk, Lina was never a police priority. And did Lina's VioGÃ©n assessment have an impact on the court's decision to deny her a restraining order against her ex-partner?
Image caption,
Judge Maria del Carmen GutiÃ©rrez sits in Malaga's gender violence court
Court authorities didn't give us permission to meet the judge who denied Lina an injunction against her ex-partner - a woman attacked on social media after Lina's death.

data.author: gozzoo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11升级中的安全要求和兼容性问题

不同观点：
• [支持升级和安全要求] 
  - [4rt] 认为强制升级到Windows 11并遵循现代安全卫生标准是必要的，即使需要强力推行。
  
• [转向Linux]
  - [conartist6] 表示在使用Windows作为主要桌面操作系统25年后，决定转向Linux，主要是为了运行Steam。这表明部分用户因Windows 11的升级要求而选择其他操作系统。

• [硬件兼容性问题]
  - [Neywiny] 提到其Win10桌面的TPM模块在Win11检测中仍不被接受，且其第六代CPU可能过旧。这反映了一些用户在升级Windows 11时遇到的硬件兼容性问题，并考虑使用绕过检测的解决方案。

• [怀疑和反感]
  - [fithisux] 对Windows 11升级要求持怀疑态度，认为文章试图说服读者接受这些要求的方式让人感到不安，甚至用了一个连环杀手的名字来加强其反对态度。

补充讨论：
- 部分用户对Windows 11的硬件要求和安全检查机制表示支持，认为这是现代安全的必要措施。
- 一些用户因升级要求而选择其他操作系统，如Linux。
- 用户面临的具体技术问题，如TPM模块和CPU兼容性，导致对升级过程的困扰和不满。
- 对微软推广Windows 11策略的怀疑和反感，反映出部分用户对强制性要求的抵触情绪。
